clue.text: Ask for contributions to authorise admitting boater?

parts.note: to authorise a measure is to pass it
something admitting a boater goes round the hat, as a hatband or a head does; read cryptically, the phrase describes surrounding a straw hat

explanation.surface: A request for donations to approve letting in someone in a straw hat, or perhaps a rower.
explanation.walkthrough: A boater is a flat-topped straw hat; whatever admits it must go all the way round that hat. 'Boater' also tempts a reading as someone in a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Collecting money by handing a hat from person to person is the idiom for asking a group to chip in.

clue.text: One in Switzerland hired out?

indicators.note: in says the letter for one sits within the other letters

parts.note: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland
a property hired out is let
one is A, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A riddle about something in Switzerland that is rented to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a Swiss holiday home that is let out.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss wooden mountain house, often rented by skiers and holidaymakers, is exactly what the clue describes.

clue.text: A sexual partner receiving drug and a healing plant

indicators.note: receiving means the partner takes the drug letter inside

parts.note: a lover is a sexual partner
E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A lover is handed drugs along with something medicinal from the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: This succulent's gel is widely used to soothe burns and skin, so it is a plant valued for healing.

clue.text: Mark hint: coastline getting rocky around top of major French commune

parts.note: M is short for mark, the old German currency

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the next piece
rocky means unsteady, so the letters are shaken into a new order
top of a down clue word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tip-off that the shoreline turns craggy near something important in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' is the old German currency, not a sign; 'getting rocky' scrambles the next two words, and 'around' wraps them about the head of 'major'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tidal island with its abbey off the Normandy coast is a commune of France.

clue.text: Repeated hostility, switching pair of characters around in film

indicators.note: around means the earlier letters wrap round the next word of the clue

parts.note: something repeated is doubled
taken as written

indicators.note: two adjacent letters of the word for hostility swap places

parts.note: enmity is hostility

explanation.surface: A film plot of feuding twice over, with two people trading places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching pair of characters' swaps the middle two consonants of the word for hostility; 'around' puts 'in' after the D of the doubled word, so 'in' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy Wilder's 1944 film noir about insurance fraud bears this title.

clue.text: Press Conservative about one of some satirical comments

indicators.note: about means the letters go round the one

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A newspaper of the right comments on a sarcastic remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like the newspapers but is the verb to iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Satirical remarks say the opposite of what is meant, which is the mark of irony.

clue.text: Wrong, we hear — no guy picked up spice

indicators.note: we hear signals the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a wrong is a sin

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means the letters run upwards, so they are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: Someone mishears a word, then a spice is collected with nobody about.
explanation.definitionFit: This bark, ground or in sticks, is one of the commonest culinary spices.

clue.text: Leave tents to be set out in further shop

parts.note: to leave is to depart

indicators.note: in puts the reordered letters inside the next word

parts.note: further means more

indicators.note: tents set out are pitched in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Campers are told to go and pitch their tents further along, at a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges 'tents' and 'in' sits that jumble after the first letter of the word for further; 'to be' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A large shop selling many kinds of goods in separate sections is this kind of store.

clue.text: Unusually methodical, I will include quartet in oratorio

indicators.note: will include means the scrambled letters take in the next piece
unusually says these letters appear in an unusual order

parts.note: a quartet is four

explanation.surface: An oddly systematic singer insists on bringing a quartet into a choral work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges 'methodical' and 'I', and 'will include' takes the number word in; the result is a Michael Tippett oratorio.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Tippett's oratorio of 1939-41 carries this title.

clue.text: Very engaged in waterway, experiencing liquidity

indicators.note: engaged in means placed inside

parts.note: the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England

explanation.surface: Someone deeply involved on a channel, finding everything fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SOLENT is the busy sailing channel off Southampton.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm with enough liquid funds to pay its debts is said to be financially sound in this sense.

clue.text: Graduate welcoming grandma into Australia in stroke of good fortune

indicators.note: welcoming means the graduate's letters take others inside

parts.note: BA is Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

indicators.note: into means the grandmother goes inside

parts.note: Oz is the informal name for Australia
nan is a familiar word for grandma

explanation.surface: A graduate gets to bring their grandmother to Australia: what luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden source of great wealth or luck, originally a rich vein of ore, is a windfall.

clue.text: Looking to benefit where some car purchase discussions focus?

definitions.meaning: someone looking to benefit is out for personal gain

definitions.text: where some car purchase discussions focus?
definitions.meaning: buyers of a car talk about its brand, Ford or Fiat, so discussions sit on that topic

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an opportunist seeking profit, while read literally the words place talk on the car's brand.

clue.text: Company encountered reindeer?

parts.note: encountered means met

explanation.surface: A firm runs into a reindeer.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an example: this is one of Santa's reindeer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the poem A Visit from St Nicholas, one of Santa's sleigh-pulling deer bears this name.

clue.text: Nineteen canapés ordered in a tidy way

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Nineteen nibbles are requested, neatly arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like placing a request for canapés but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The old saying for being very neat and orderly compares a person to a bright silver coin.

clue.text: Views you picked up in part of Wales

parts.note: angles are views or points of view

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means the letters rise, read backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: Someone's opinions are collected in a corner of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' tempts a sound-alike reading, but here it reverses YE.
explanation.definitionFit: The large island off the north-west Welsh coast is a county of Wales.

clue.text: Concertgoers in favour of silent performers? Not I

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: not means the letter after it is removed

parts.note: mimers act without words

explanation.surface: Music lovers who prefer mime acts, though the speaker is not one.
explanation.walkthrough: These are audiences at the Proms, the BBC's summer classical concert season in London.
explanation.definitionFit: People attending the Proms, the London summer concerts, are known by this name.

clue.text: Fast up the pole?

definitions.meaning: up the pole is old British slang for drunk

explanation.definitionFit: A knot held fast is firm and secure, and the word is also informal British slang for drunk.

clue.text: Flying Tardis? Here's lots of notes

definitions.note: plural: groups of three notes each

indicators.note: the Tardis flying through time and space scrambles its letters

explanation.surface: Doctor Who's time machine in flight makes a lot of noise.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tardis is the Doctor's time machine in the British TV series Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: Chords made of three notes stacked in thirds are the musical sense of the word, so groups of notes.

clue.text: No soldiers returned in film — my recollection's very clear

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters inside

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, such as a mist

indicators.note: returned means read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
men are soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: A veteran remembers a war film in which no soldiers came home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' is a cinema film on the surface, but here a thin haze. The definition is what this person would say.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer with a trained, exceptional memory could say their recall is crystal clear.

clue.text: Area of Europe resembling part of Russia within its borders

indicators.note: only what lies inside the edge of the Russian region is kept, losing its opening letter

parts.note: Siberia is the vast Asian part of Russia

explanation.surface: A European region said to look like part of Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: The European name sits inside the Russian one, which 'resembling' hints at; only the S is dropped, so 'its borders' is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula holding Spain and Portugal is the south-western region of Europe.

clue.text: Mournful English cricket side, by one account

parts.note: the leg side is the half of a cricket field behind the batter's legs
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A sad tale of an English cricket team, as told by one person.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the leg side and the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry of lament for the dead is called elegy, so the adjective means sorrowful.

clue.text: Least able to sense university doctor entering home

indicators.note: entering means going inside

parts.note: a nest is a home
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: The college doctor comes into a house where the patient feels nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbness is a loss of feeling, so the most numb is the one feeling least.

clue.text: Dog's energy restrained by perturbed breeder/trainer

indicators.note: restrained by means held inside
perturbed means agitated, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dog's high spirits are reined in by its anxious handler.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scottish breed, also called the Scottie, is a breed of small dog.
